newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, snap winning streak.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, snap winning streak.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended weaker on Tuesday, as investors reaped profits after three sessions of record closes.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index finished 48.59 points lower at 6442.54, off its session low of 6420.67.
Market players rearranged their portfolios after Toronto posted its 15th record close of the year on Monday.
"A bit of back and fill in Canada after a big day yesterday, but nothing too terrifying," said Dunnery Best, director of private client investing at brokerage Midland Walwyn.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors headed lower, led by consumer products, oils, pipelines and conglomerates. Golds, retail, industrial products and forestry products strengthened.
Heavyweight financial issues generally lost ground after the first two of Canada's big six banks reported record second-quarter earnings, which matched analysts' expectations, Best said.
Turnover in Canada's largest equities market was active at 92.4 million shares worth C$1.6 billion ($1.15 billion).
Declining issues beat out advancing ones 580 to 413, while 323 issues closed level.
In individual stocks, Bank of Montreal, Canada's third largest, dipped 1.15 to 53.90 after reporting second-quarter earnings of C$1.11 a share versus year-ago C$0.98.
Bank of Nova Scotia, the country's fourth biggest bank, rose 0.15 to 58.95 after second-quarter earnings of C$1.16, compared to year earlier C$1.01.
Barrick Gold Corp., the world's third largest gold miner, rose 0.95 to 35.20, topping Toronto actives on two million shares.
Computer linking firm Newbridge Networks Corp. rose 2.50 to 57.50 as momentum in U.S. high-technology stocks spread to Canada.
